meta.title: Night Bazaar Chiang Mai (ไนท์บาซาร์เชียงใหม่) | Chiang Mai, Thailand | The city's largest night market & craft landmark by the Mae Ping River
meta.description: The complete guide to Night Bazaar Chiang Mai: along Changklan Road on the east bank of the Mae Ping River, it is one of northern Thailand's biggest and most iconic night markets. Handicrafts, original design, street food and live music come together here, open daily from 18:00, free entry — your gateway to Chiang Mai after dark.

mission.title: About this guide
mission.text: We want every traveler to Chiang Mai to understand Changklan Road before nightfall — how it went from a Lanna-era elephant-tethering ground to tonight's glowing night-market promenade. We gathered scattered official info, local stories and practical tips into this guide, so your 'market visit' becomes a real Chiang Mai night out.

sunsetPlanner.eyebrow: Golden window for your night out
sunsetPlanner.title: Sunset & blue hour
sunsetPlanner.note: Arrive about 60 minutes before sunset. Roughly 30 minutes after sunset the stall lights switch on — prime time for photos and strolling. The blue hour (about 20–30 min after sunset) frames sky and neon together, most photogenic.
sunsetPlanner.seaGlare: Lighting tip: about 30 minutes after sunset the whole Changklan Road lights up; warm bulbs and neon signage are at their best.
sunsetPlanner.tideTip: Crowd tip: 19:00–21:00 is peak. To avoid the crush, come right at 18:00 opening or after 21:30 as crowds thin.

intro.title: Meet Night Bazaar Chiang Mai
intro.description: Night Bazaar Chiang Mai is one of northern Thailand's most representative night markets, spreading along Changklan Road on the east bank of the Mae Ping River. It packs Lanna handicrafts, original design, street food and live performance into one promenade: a normal street by day, it transforms after dark into a glowing night-life landmark. Free entry, open daily — the easiest and most memorable entry to Chiang Mai after dark.

visitGuide.title: How to get the most out of it
visitGuide.description: Treat the bazaar as a combo of 'slow browse + eat + hunt for goods', not a race.

items.text: Main street first, alleys later: main street for lights and souvenirs, alleys (Anusarn) more local and cheaper.
Save room for the food street: northern BBQ, sausages, mango sticky rice and fresh juice are worth trying.
Hunt crafts slowly: Lanna silver, cotton, paper art and aromatherapy are often negotiable — compare three shops.

humanities.subtitle: From a Lanna elephant-tethering ground to tonight's glowing night-market promenade.

knowledge.title: History & stories of Night Bazaar Chiang Mai

sections.title: Lanna era: 'Changkhlan', the elephant stake
sections.content: 'Chang Khlan' (Changklan) means 'elephant stake' in Lanna — said to be where caravans and elephant trains once tethered and rested. As the heart of the Lanna Kingdom, Chiang Mai was a trade and pilgrimage corridor between Myanmar, Laos and Siam, and Changklan Road sat on the vital path from the Old City to the Mae Ping ferry.

cards.title: Name origin
cards.text: 'Chang Khlan' literally means 'elephant stake', echoing old elephant-train rest stops.

cards.title: Lanna trade road
cards.text: Changklan linked the Old City to the river ferry — part of the ancient north–south corridor.

cards.title: Riverside settlement
cards.text: The east bank had wharves and market sprouts early, foreshadowing today's bazaar.

sections.title: Lao migrant community & the south-city layout
sections.content: In the late 18th century, when Chiang Mai's ruler Kawila rebuilt the city, he resettled a group of Lao (Lao Vieng / Lao Luang) people to the south-city area; Lao communities and temples (such as Wat Buppharam) formed around Changklan. Diverse groups lived side by side, bringing crafts, weaving and market culture — the distant root of the bazaar's 'handmade + food' character.

cards.title: Lao migrants
cards.text: Kawila's resettled Lao community shaped the south-city ethnic and craft base.

cards.title: Temples & markets
cards.text: Community temples spurred festivals and nearby markets; commerce continues today.

cards.title: Craft DNA
cards.text: Weaving, silver and paper arts from home workshops are sources of bazaar goods.

sections.title: Tourism era: the birth of the night market
sections.content: In the 1980s–90s, as Chiang Mai tourism boomed, hostels, travel agencies and craft shops along Changklan began selling unsold daytime goods in the evening. Over time stalls merged into a fixed 'night market'; the adjacent Anusarn Market and Kalare night zone took shape, and Changklan Road night market became Chiang Mai's best-known night-life landmark, written into countless travel guides.

cards.text: Evening craft stalls gradually merged into a fixed night market.

cards.title: Travel guide fame
cards.text: Featured in global guides, it became synonymous with Chiang Mai nights.

sections.title: Today's bazaar: a promenade of crafts & nightlife
sections.content: Today's Night Bazaar Chiang Mai spreads along Changklan Road, blending handicrafts, original design, clothing, aromatherapy, replica knick-knacks and street food. Its south end connects to the Loi Kroh bar street; the north mouth nears the Mae Ping and Tha Phae Gate. It is both a treasure-hunt for visitors and a place for locals to eat out, stroll and hear live music — a city promenade still growing.

didYouKnow.title: Did you know?
didYouKnow.text: The name 'Changklan' is about elephants — 'Chang' is elephant, 'Khlan' is stake/tether. In other words, today's glowing night market is named after the old Lanna tradition of tethering elephants to rest.

featured.text: The lanterns blew me away the first time — the whole street feels like an open-air party.
Crafts are richer than expected; hunt slowly and you'll find something special.

items.name: Amara K.
items.text: Walked over from Tha Phae just in time for dark — lights on, the street came alive. So many craft stalls, bargaining was fun, food street stuffed me.

items.name: Li Wen
items.text: Huge scale, easy to get lost first time. Main street then alleys; Anusarn is cheaper. Crowded but atmospheric.

items.name: Tomoko S.
items.text: Changklan in blue hour is so photogenic. Bought lots of aromatherapy and cotton. Live music nice — worth returning.

items.name: Weerapong
items.text: Locals come for late eats too. Peak season is packed; after 21:30 it's calmer and prices talk down more.
